A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pistachio benchmark. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original VAD and VAU evaluations, cross-dataset transfer and training-data experiments, and annotation-quality comparisons in its appendix.

after.justification: v6 retains these original results and adds baseline evaluations, pipeline and efficiency measurements, a human annotation study, and feature-distribution analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds optional four-step distilled generation and a TeaCache-assisted configuration, extending inference procedures. The core scene assignment, storyline construction, chained generation, filtering and annotation refinement remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that these accelerated configurations regenerated Pistachio.

E1.justification: MSAD changes from a dataset discussed in related work to an evaluated transfer target and a dataset included in feature-distribution analysis. Existing Pistachio tasks and coverage, including Cosmos, Hailuo, UCF-Crime, XD-Violence and appendix ShanghaiTech evaluations, are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds the evaluated training-free VADTree baseline while retaining the previous eight VAD methods. The VAU comparison adds InternVL3-2B, InternVL3-8B, InternVL3-14B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B variants within already represented model families.

E3.justification: v6 substantially extends evaluation design: XD-Violence-source and pooled five-dataset training, direct training-free VADTree evaluation, additional VAU model sizes, four-dimensional VLM pipeline scoring, generation-efficiency configurations, and a 100-video study with three annotators. Existing dataset splits and principal AUC/AP and F1 protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v4's qualitative pipeline comparisons, v6 adds quantitative strategy ablations in Table A.2, efficiency analysis in Table A.3, human annotation validation in Appendix B.3, and I3D feature-distribution analysis in Figure A.3. These substantially broaden evidence about generation quality, computational cost, annotation reliability and transfer.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly reports inter-annotator agreement estimates from three annotators: kappa of 0.76 at event level and 0.72 at video level. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the main VAD/VAU comparisons.

E6.justification: Matched existing scores are retained, but substantial new results cover VADTree, MSAD, XD-Violence-source and joint training, additional VAU models, and appendix analyses. VADTree reports 72.52% AUC and 25.15% AP; added InternVL3-14B becomes the VAU average leader at 29.39. Table 1 also revises MSAD's anomaly-type count from 35 to 11. Relocated statistics and earlier appendix transfer results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, their mathematical definitions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No formal theorem, proof or derivation is added; the new causal-inversion discussion is a qualitative interpretation.

C1.justification: The main benchmark and automated-construction contributions remain intact. The introduction corrects the description of all 4,962 videos as long-form, and the conclusion more explicitly positions Pistachio as a complement to real data and a foundation for fine-tuning.

C2.justification: New Section 5 substantially expands applicability limits, including surveillance-domain transfer failures and character-identity drift, with deployment guidance. New interpretations address joint training, feature-distribution overlap and training-free detection failures. Appendix B.3 also introduces the stronger assertion that annotation hallucination is structurally impossible, which the reported evidence does not establish.

D1.justification: v6 newly discloses the 3.98 filtering-score cutoff, approximately two person-days of manual filtering, and 90% normal-video versus 80% anomaly-video acceptance rates. It also supplies acceleration timings and VRAM figures and describes VADTree processing. Core model choices, construction hardware and the project-access location are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds references for VideoScore and VADTree and discusses the latter's training-free approach through its evaluation. Existing cited works and the broader positioning against collected VAD datasets and video-generation research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained. Local revisions correct the abstract/introduction ordering, update author information and headers, rewrite portions of experimental interpretation and the conclusion, introduce a dedicated limitations section, and reorganize appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v6 adds two compact appendix tables and a t-SNE figure, expands comparison tables, and revises Figure 2's assignment-stage display. Dataset statistics move from main Table 5 to Table A.5, while existing appendix figures and tables are reordered. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: Expanded comparisons, human annotation checks and concrete deployment limits provide a modest net improvement over v4's thinner validation and brief domain-gap caveat. Gains are limited by underspecified new study protocols and new overclaims: annotation hallucination is not shown impossible, and joint-training MSAD AP of 25.69 trails Pistachio-only 54.24 despite the claim of strongest performance across all benchmarks.
